Safely delete subplot observation features

safe_delete_subplot_obs_features.Rd

**DANGER: This permanently deletes data from the database!**

Deletes records of `data_subplot_feat`: the features that describe a subplot, such as the people of a census (`team_leader`, `additional_people`, ...). Nothing references `data_subplot_feat`, so only the selected records are removed. **Subplots and plots are preserved.**

**Safety features:** - Dry-run mode to preview what will be deleted - Requires explicit confirmation (unless force = TRUE) - Uses a database transaction (rollback on error)

Usage

safe_delete_subplot_obs_features(
  id_subplot_feat = NULL,
  subplot_ids = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  con = NULL,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  force = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

id_subplot_feat

Integer vector. Specific record ID(s) to delete (`id_subplot_feat` from `data_subplot_feat`). Takes precedence over `subplot_ids` / `types`. Typically obtained from query_plot_features(..., format = "long", include_subplot_obs_features = TRUE)$subplot_obs_features. Default NULL.

subplot_ids

Integer vector. Delete all observation features of these subplot(s) (`id_sub_plots` from `data_liste_sub_plots`). Can be combined with `types`. Default NULL.

types

Character vector. Restrict to these feature types (`type` from `subplotype_list`, e.g. `"additional_people"`). Only used with `subplot_ids`. Default NULL (all types).

con

Database connection. If NULL, will connect automatically.

dry_run

Logical. If TRUE, shows what would be deleted without deleting. Default TRUE for safety.

force

Logical. If TRUE, skips confirmation prompts. Default FALSE. **USE WITH EXTREME CAUTION!**

verbose

Logical. Show detailed progress? Default TRUE.

Value

List with deletion summary (invisible). Includes `feat_info`, a data frame with one row per record to be deleted (`id_subplot_feat`, `id_sub_plots`, `type`, `typevalue`, `typevalue_char`, `colnam`), and `error`, the database message, when the deletion failed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- call.mydb()

# STEP 1: Extract the records and pick the ones to remove
obs <- query_plot_features(subplot_ids = 15063, format = "long",
                           include_subplot_obs_features = TRUE,
                           con = con)$subplot_obs_features
ids_to_remove <- obs$id_subplot_feat[obs$colnam == "Some Person"]

# STEP 2: Always do a dry-run first!
safe_delete_subplot_obs_features(id_subplot_feat = ids_to_remove, con = con)

# STEP 3: Review output, then delete if sure
safe_delete_subplot_obs_features(id_subplot_feat = ids_to_remove,
                                 con = con, dry_run = FALSE)

# Alternative: every additional_people record of a census
safe_delete_subplot_obs_features(subplot_ids = 15063,
                                 types = "additional_people", con = con)
} # }
